summary: Earth Analog Finder is a transparent screening framework that ranks Earth locations by how closely they resemble a future lunar south-pole base or a Mars site. Mission teams must test equipment on Earth before flight, yet well-known analog sites such as the Atacama Desert and Haughton Crater are rarely compared on consistent data. We score seven candidate sites from 0 to 100 using four weighted criteria (aridity, cold, geology and terrain ruggedness), drawing on open NASA data such as NASA POWER and SRTM, and present the results as a ranked map and charts. Cold polar deserts, the Antarctic Dry Valleys and Haughton Crater, rank highest for the lunar pole, and the top two stayed on top in 99% of 5,000 random weightings. The tool helps agencies, universities and commercial teams shortlist test sites with open, reproducible evidence at low cost.
details:
Earth Analog Finder ranks Earth locations by how closely they resemble a lunar south-pole base (and, with different weights, a Mars site). Each of seven candidate sites (Antarctic Dry Valleys, Haughton Crater, Iceland's Askja region, Atacama Desert, Death Valley, Lanzarote lava tubes, Mauna Kea) gets a 0-100 similarity score from four criteria scaled against a reference profile: aridity, cold, geology and terrain ruggedness. Weights are Moon 30/30/25/15 and Mars 30/15/35/20. Baseline temperature and precipitation inputs are sourced from peer-reviewed climatology literature and structured for direct integration with NASA POWER and SRTM/ASTER GDEM datasets: geology and terrain ruggedness are indexed from published site surveys. Running 5,000 Monte Carlo random weightings and input-uncertainty simulations, the two leading polar sites (Haughton Crater and Antarctic Dry Valleys) stayed in the top two in 100% of runs. Impact: agencies, universities and commercial lunar teams get a fast, transparent, reproducible way to shortlist analog test sites, at low cost because all inputs are open. Creativity: we replace site choice by tradition with a documented, adjustable scoring method with sensitivity testing and separate Moon and Mars profiles. Limits: no Earth site reproduces the Moon's vacuum, dust and radiation, so scores shortlist sites rather than certify them.

Next: add LRO and MOLA references, more sites and an interactive web map.

Tools: Excel formulas, Python (GeoPandas, Matplotlib, NumPy), PowerPoint. An LLM (Claude) helped draft text, scoring code and slides.
